thread_analysis.thread_summary: Ricoh Imaging (contact Hirokazu Maeda, later joined by senior contact Kenji Daigo) engages Allion (Masaya Iida, Toshitaka Mochizuki, Itsuo Sakai) for a combined USB/DisplayPort/Bluetooth certification project for a camera product, spanning roughly November 2024 through July 2025. The thread covers early-stage USB-IF/DisplayPort certification scoping, an end-to-end Bluetooth SIG registration process walkthrough, basic Bluetooth ICS onboarding, AutomationExplorer pre-test tool capability/limitation clarification, registration timeline/confidentiality planning, and culminates in an extended, escalating RF PHY Power Class 1 vs. Class 2 reference-module registration dispute that traced through Japan Radio Law evidence, a SAR-compliance/antenna-size engineering explanation for why the camera's real output power differs from the module vendor's own datasheet power, confirmation that SIG-registered Power Class is a ceiling not a floor, and a critical post-July-2024 inter-layer consistency check that made independent re-registration impractical for a set-maker without IC-level source access.
all_questions_found: Is there a standalone PD-only logo certification, and can a single passing mode (rather than both dual modes) yield logo certification? (see thread_0006_case_01)
Is 500mA sufficient Source current for PD compliance, or is 900mA the true minimum? (see thread_0006_case_02)
Can a camera prototype with sub-threshold Source current still get UFP-only (sink-only) certification, especially given its need for DisplayPort Source functionality? (see thread_0006_case_03)
What is DIS ICS, and who should fill it out? (see thread_0006_case_04)

What does 'desired certification acquisition date' mean, what is the process/timeline after RF/RF PHY test pass (including proxy payment lead time and test/payment ordering flexibility), and how to keep a launch date confidential? (see thread_0006_case_05)

Our product's RF PHY test result is Class 2, but the module's reference QDID is registered Class 1 -- is that legally invalid under Japan's Radio Law, why does our real output differ from the module vendor's own datasheet power, must our registration match the module's Class exactly, and can we just test and register independently instead? (see thread_0006_case_06)
Now that the pre-test kickoff meeting is done, what does the complete registration process look like end-to-end, including final Compliance Folder document requirements? (see thread_0006_case_07)

Does passing AutomationExplorer's basic command checks (in Serial-Two-Wire mode) guarantee formal RF PHY test success, is the tool limited to 1M PHY mode only, and are fixed (non-configurable) DTM test parameters acceptable? (see thread_0006_case_08)

(Logistics, not separately cased) Equipment list and shipping/export-document clarifications (UART vs USB cable count, SMA connector, export classification opinion document, battery-not-included supply voltage note), invoice/payment timing, test sample shipment scheduling, and an internal-only equipment calibration scheduling compliance discussion (ISO 17025 / internal calibration policy) -- routine project administration or internal-only operational content without a generalizable customer-facing lesson.
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: The thread's most valuable technical content is the multi-stage RF PHY Power Class dispute (case_06), which ultimately surfaces four distinct, generalizable lessons stacked on top of each other: SIG registration and national radio law are independent regimes; a SIG-registered Power Class is a ceiling, not a required floor; real-world engineering constraints (SAR limits, antenna size) can legitimately force a product's actual output well below an upstream module's datasheet power; and the post-July-2024 registration system's strengthened inter-layer consistency checking can make independent re-registration impractical for a set-maker who treats an upstream IC layer as a black box. Case_08 (AutomationExplorer) and case_07 (end-to-end process overview) are also strong, previously-undocumented additions found only by reading every message's new content directly rather than relying on keyword search.
thread_analysis.key_decision_logic: See thread_0006_case_01 through thread_0006_case_08 for case-specific decision logic; the throughline is that registration-site/ICS mechanics (what can be Included, what Power Class is declared, what inter-layer consistency rules currently apply) must be evaluated separately from each country's legal/regulatory output power constraints, from a product's own real-world engineering constraints, and from the certification program's all-or-nothing mode coverage rules.
thread_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: See individual case files; the highest-risk item is case_06, where conflating SIG registration validity with national radio-law compliance, or failing to check the current registration system's inter-layer consistency rules before recommending independent re-registration, could have caused a much longer dispute, a dead-end registration attempt, or unnecessary cost.
thread_analysis.consulting_mistake: The module manufacturer ('M company') repeatedly failed to directly answer the customer's escalating questions about Class 2-only registration availability, requiring multiple rounds of the same request before finally surfacing the no-cost IC-vendor Subset DN alternative. This redo pass (reading every message's new content directly rather than relying on keyword-pattern search) found that the original case_06 write-up, while accurate as far as it went, was substantially incomplete: it stopped before the later messages revealed the actual engineering reason for the power mismatch, the ceiling-vs-floor clarification, and the critical inter-layer consistency obstacle to independent re-registration -- all of which fundamentally changed the practical recommendation. This is a concrete illustration of why partial-thread reading risks producing a plausible-but-incomplete answer.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: When a customer raises a national-radio-law-based legal objection to a module's Bluetooth SIG Power Class registration, resolve the conceptual confusion (SIG registration vs. national radio law are independent regimes, and SIG Power Class is a ceiling not a floor) early and explicitly; when a set-maker proposes testing and registering independently instead of referencing an upstream module, proactively check whether the current registration system's inter-layer consistency rules would require retesting a black-box layer they cannot access, since that can silently foreclose an otherwise-reasonable-looking option; and proactively surface all available resolution paths together rather than one at a time.
